families.imported-indifference-instrumen.formal: The framework forbids uncaused structure: a construction may not carry distinctions (partitions, assignments, orderings) that nothing in the framework determines; it is a structural premise of the series, not a theorem, and is flagged as such wherever it is used. The reading this paper makes of it, stated here so that it can be examined: the instrument equates weights along symmetry orbits and forbids selections nothing causes; it never equates norms between inequivalent irreducible components, which no symmetry relates. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}, with the principality of the fuzzy sphere \cite[Thm.~5.5]{ButlerT8} as the use of it that the proof there requires; the reading is this paper's.
families.imported-indifference-instrumen.technical:
Indifference is the series' structural premise, not a theorem: no construction may carry a distinction (a partition, an assignment, an ordering) that nothing in the framework determines. This Fact imports that premise and fixes how it is read when used as an instrument on weights.

The reading has two halves. Positively, it equates weights along symmetry orbits: if a symmetry $g$ of the framework relates components $c$ and $g \cdot c$, then $w(g \cdot c) = w(c)$, and it forbids any selection among them that nothing causes. Negatively, it never equates norms between inequivalent irreducible components, since no symmetry relates them. The reading is the families paper's own, stated so that it can be examined, and every use of it is flagged as resting on the premise.
families.imported-indifference-instrumen.lay: The series assumes that nature does not make arbitrary choices: if nothing in the theory tells two things apart, the theory may not treat them differently. This entry says how the families paper itself reads that assumption in practice. Things related by a symmetry must be given equal weight, but things that are genuinely different are never forced to match. It is an assumption of the programme, not something it proves.

__notes__.note.families.indifference-route-examine: The natural candidate explanation of the angle is an equal split of the vacuum norm between the $S_{3}$ singlet and doublet by indifference, giving $\cos^{2}\theta = \tfrac12$, exactly Koide. The reading of Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument} closes this route: the instrument equates weights along symmetry orbits and forbids uncaused selections; it does not equate norms between inequivalent irreducible components, which no symmetry relates. Applied to face space it says what Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one} already extracted: the uncaused vacuum lies wholly in the singlet. The route is withdrawn, and what survives is a measurement: the physical $\sqrt{m}$ vector splits its norm between singlet and doublet as $941.55 : 941.55$, equality to seven parts in $10^{6}$, an order-one, exactly tuned, \emph{caused} breaking whose cause is the open target. The breaking is small in $m$ and large in $\sqrt{m}$, compatible because masses are squares.

one-relation.imported-indifference-instr.technical:
Indifference is a structural premise of the series, not a theorem: a construction may not carry distinctions that nothing in the framework determines. This Fact imports it together with the families paper's reading of it as an instrument, which equates weights along exact symmetry orbits, $w(g \cdot c) = w(c)$ for an exact symmetry $g$, forbids uncaused selections, and never equates inequivalent irreducible components.

Two clauses are attached here. The moduli clause says that genuine moduli are data, not something the instrument smooths away; it is the reading half of the weight-moduli Fact and holds at observation level there. The indexicality clause says that the question why ours is the visible sector has no dynamical answer; it is the dark-matter paper's premise form of indifference, scoped there to the reversal orbit. Every use of the instrument in this paper is flagged as resting on the premise.
one-relation.imported-indifference-instr.lay: The series assumes that nature does not make arbitrary choices: if nothing in the theory tells two things apart, the theory may not treat them differently. In use, this means giving equal weight to things related by an exact symmetry, while never forcing genuinely different things to match. Numbers the theory leaves free are treated as facts to be measured rather than averaged away (a reading held at observation level), and the question of why we find ourselves in our sector rather than its mirror is treated as a matter of where we stand rather than of dynamics. All of this is an assumption of the programme, not a result.

scrambling.indifference-structural-premi.formal: The framework forbids uncaused structure: a construction may not carry distinctions (partitions, assignments, orderings) that nothing in the framework determines. \emph{Provenance and level:} this is the structural principle used to order the family faces, applied here at the declared level; it is a premise of the derivation below, not a theorem, and is flagged as such.
scrambling.indifference-structural-premi.technical:
The principle of indifference forbids uncaused structure: a construction may not carry distinctions, such as partitions, assignments or orderings, that nothing in the framework determines. Concretely, if the framework supplies no datum that singles out one partition $n = n_1 + \dots + n_k$ of a set of modes over another, a construction may not rely on such a partition.

It is a premise, not a theorem, applied at the declared level and flagged wherever it is used. It is the principle used to order the family faces, and here it is the premise of the derivation that selects the principal embedding for the boundary modes.
scrambling.indifference-structural-premi.lay: This is an assumption, not a result: the theory may not build in distinctions that nothing in it explains. If the theory gives no reason to split things into groups, or to label one of them first, then no construction is allowed to do so. The series uses this rule repeatedly and marks each place where it does.

synthesis.indifference-is-curie-plus-sin.formal:
Formalise the indifference premise (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}, in the reading of Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument}) as follows. A finite group $G$ acts on a set $D$ of framework data and on a finite set $X$ of components; $G_d$ is the stabiliser of the actual datum $d$. A \emph{construction} is a map $\Phi$ from $D$ to nonempty sets of weight assignments $f : X \to \R$ that is covariant, $\Phi(g d) = g \cdot \Phi(d)$ (it uses nothing but the datum); it is \emph{single-valued} at $d$ if $\Phi(d)$ has one element.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Curie.)} $\Phi(d)$ is $G_d$-invariant. If $\Phi$ is single-valued at $d$, its assignment is constant on $G_d$-orbits and it singles out no element, partition or ordering of $X$ that $G_d$ does not fix: the clauses ``equates along symmetry orbits'' and ``forbids selections nothing causes''.
\item \emph{(No licence across orbits.)} The equalities $f(x) = f(y)$ holding for every $G_d$-invariant $f$ are exactly those with $y \in G_d x$, so the clause ``never equates inequivalent components'' is a theorem about what invariance licenses. On a finite orbit the only invariant probability is the uniform one (Haar measure); maximum entropy over all of $X$ is invariant but equates across orbits, so it is strictly stronger than symmetry.
\item \emph{(Residue.)} Without single-valuedness the conclusions of (1) fail: under the swap of a two-element orbit the outcome set of the two selections is invariant and contains no invariant member. Indifference is covariance plus single-valuedness, and single-valuedness is all that it adds to symmetry.
\item \emph{(P2.)} For the towers, $G_d$ is generated by the reversal $(p,q) \mapsto (q,p)$, acting on residues as $r \mapsto -r$ with orbits $\{0\}, \{4\}, \{1,7\}, \{2,6\}, \{3,5\}$. Each equality P2 asserts along $\{2,6\}$ (common ceiling coupling, common asymmetry per mode) is an instance of (1) for one datum, so under this formalisation it holds exactly when the descent is covariant and single-valued in that datum. Applied to the deposited energy per unit charge, the same reasoning gives a common temperature, which the record excludes (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}); so the cold mirror requires the descent to be many-valued, or not reversal covariant, in that datum. P2's indexical clause (which of $2$, $6$ is visible) does not supply this: read as a fact about the observer's location it leaves the descent single-valued, and read as a fact about the descent's outcome it is already a case of many-valuedness that P2 must then admit datum by datum.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.indifference-is-curie-plus-sin.technical:
The series' principle of indifference forbids distinctions that nothing in the framework determines, and is used to equate weights along symmetry orbits. Model a construction as a covariant map from the framework's data to sets of possible outcomes; reading an uncaused distinction as a failure of covariance is a modelling choice, and everything below is relative to it, for a finite symmetry group acting on a finite set of components carrying weights. If the outcome is unique, Curie's principle applies: a unique outcome of symmetric data is symmetric, so weights are equal along orbits and nothing is selected that the symmetry does not fix. The companion clause, that indifference never equates inequivalent components, then needs no premise: the indicator function of an orbit is invariant and separates it from every other orbit, so invariance alone licenses exactly the equalities within orbits. In weight form this is Haar measure on each finite orbit; maximum entropy over the whole set would equate across orbits and is stronger than symmetry.

For weights on finite orbits, what indifference adds to symmetry is therefore single-valuedness of the outcome. This does not cover the use of indifference that selects a structure rather than weights, the principal embedding: there the only single-valued covariant output is the zero map, and selecting the principal embedding takes a measure principle in addition (filed alongside, synthesis.principality-is-genericity). When the outcome is a set (as with spontaneous symmetry breaking), the set is symmetric but no member need be. For the towers, each equality P2 draws between the two reversal partners needs single-valuedness in that datum; the excluded common mirror temperature is a datum where it must fail. P2's indexical clause, which partner is visible, does not by itself make room for that: as a fact about where the observer stands it leaves the descent single-valued, and as a fact about the outcome it is already the many-valuedness that P2 would then have to admit datum by datum.
synthesis.indifference-is-curie-plus-sin.lay: The series often argues that two things must be equal because nothing in the theory could tell them apart. This result makes that argument precise and finds its exact cost. If a process has only one possible outcome and treats two things symmetrically, the outcome must treat them alike: that part is just symmetry. But if the process can end in several ways, each individual ending can favour one side, as a ball balanced on a hilltop must roll one way or the other. The extra assumption hidden in the principle is that the outcome was unique. Applied to the two mirror worlds of the series, each equality drawn between them needs its own uniqueness assumption, and the evidence that the mirror world is colder than ours shows that, for its temperature at least, the outcome was lopsided.

proofs.main:
\emph{(1)} For $g \in G_d$, $g\cdot\Phi(d) = \Phi(gd) = \Phi(d)$: the outcome set is $G_d$-invariant. If it is a single assignment $f$, then $g \cdot f = f$ for every $g \in G_d$, where $(g\cdot f)(x) = f(g^{-1}x)$; so $f(g^{-1}x) = f(x)$ and $f$ is constant on orbits. Any element, partition or ordering of $X$ read off from $f$ alone is then fixed by $G_d$, since $f$ is; a selection of one element of a nontrivial orbit, or an ordering of an orbit, is not.

\emph{(2)} If $y \in G_d x$, every invariant $f$ has $f(y) = f(x)$. If $y \notin G_d x$, the indicator $\chi$ of the orbit $G_d x$ is invariant (an orbit is carried to itself) and $\chi(x) = 1 \neq 0 = \chi(y)$. So the common equalities of all invariant assignments are the orbit relations, no more. The invariant assignments are the image of the averaging projection $f \mapsto |G_d|^{-1}\sum_g g\cdot f$, of dimension equal to the number of orbits. A probability on one finite orbit that is invariant is constant on it, hence uniform: this is the push-forward of Haar measure on $G_d$ under an orbit map. The uniform distribution on all of $X$, the maximum of entropy with no constraint, is invariant (permutations preserve it) and assigns equal weight to points of different orbits; so maximum entropy imposes equalities that invariance does not license. At prescribed orbit totals the invariant assignment is unique, the total spread uniformly over each orbit.

\emph{(3)} Let $G_d = \{1, s\}$ swap $X = \{x, y\}$ and $\Phi(d) = \{(1,0), (0,1)\}$, the two selections. Then $s \cdot \Phi(d) = \Phi(d)$, so covariance holds at $d$ (and $\Phi$ extends covariantly to the orbit of $d$ in any $D$), while neither member is invariant. The same holds for the cyclic group on three labels and its three selections. Hence (1) uses single-valuedness essentially, and adding single-valuedness to covariance gives back every clause of the reading in Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument} by (1) and (2). Conversely, a single-valued covariant construction always exists on these data (for instance the barycentre of any invariant outcome set, itself invariant), so the two inputs are independent: covariance does not imply single-valuedness, and single-valuedness alone imposes nothing without covariance.

\emph{(4)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one} the residue $r = p - q \bmod 8$ is an invariant of the soldered algebra, so the towers' data distinguish residues; the reversal $(p,q) \mapsto (q,p)$ sends $r$ to $-r$, and the check computes its orbits on residues from the signatures with $p, q \leq 4$: $\{0\}, \{1,7\}, \{2,6\}, \{3,5\}, \{4\}$. P2 equates along the reversal only. Each equality it draws on $\{2,6\}$ is an instance of (1) for one datum (a weight assignment on the two towers), so it holds under the formalisation exactly when the descent is covariant and single-valued in that datum. For the deposited energy per unit charge, single-valuedness with covariance gives $T' = T$, which Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} records as excluded; so for that datum one of the two fails. The indexical clause admits two readings. As a fact about the observer's position, it is not an output of the descent and leaves the descent single-valued, so it does not accommodate the cold mirror. As a fact about the descent's outcome, it selects one member of a nontrivial orbit, which by (1) no single-valued covariant construction produces, so it is itself a case of many-valuedness, and then (3) shows that the equalities for the other data no longer follow from symmetry and must be supplied datum by datum.

\emph{Scope.} Everything above concerns weight assignments on a finite set with a finite symmetry group. For the use of indifference that selects an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ structure on the boundary-mode matrix algebra, clause (1) applied pointwise gives only the zero map as a single-valued covariant output, so the principal embedding is not obtained by single-valuedness; it needs a measure principle on the space of structures (filed alongside, synthesis.principality-is-genericity).

synthesis.principality-is-genericity.formal:
Let $\Mat_n$ be the matrix algebra of the boundary modes (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}) and classify $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ structures on it by the partition $\lambda$ of $n$ (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-partition-data}(i)), equivalently by the conjugacy class of the nilpotent element $e_\lambda$ of a standard triple; the zero map has $\lambda = (1^n)$, the principal embedding $\lambda = (n)$. Write $m_d$ for the number of parts of size $d$ and $\lambda^{T}$ for the conjugate partition.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Invariance.)} The conjugation orbit of $e_\lambda$ has dimension $n^2 - \sum_i (\lambda^{T}_i)^2$. It is a single point exactly for $\lambda = (1^n)$: the only $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ structure fixed pointwise by the symmetry of the matrix algebra ($\operatorname{Ad}_g \circ \phi = \phi$ for every invertible $g$) is the zero map. (Fixed only as a subalgebra, the principal image is also fixed at $n = 2$, where it is all of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$.)
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Indistinguishable blocks.)} The commutant of the image of a standard triple has dimension $\sum_d m_d^2$; it permutes the blocks of each size transitively, and blocks of different sizes are told apart by their dimension. So no block is distinguished from another exactly when $\lambda = (k^{n/k})$ is rectangular, $k \mid n$. For $n$ prime this leaves the principal embedding and the zero map; for composite $n$ every rectangular type, for example $(2,2)$ at $n = 4$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Genericity.)} The orbit dimension equals $n^2 - n$ exactly for $\lambda = (n)$ and is strictly smaller for every other $\lambda$. The nilpotent cone is the union of the finitely many orbits, so the principal orbit is open and dense in it, and for every measure on the cone absolutely continuous with respect to its conjugation-invariant measure class, the type is $(n)$ almost surely.
\end{enumerate}
So the selection of the principal embedding in Theorem \claimref{scrambling.principality-indifference-sphere} does not follow from symmetry: pointwise invariance selects the zero map, and the absence of distinguished blocks allows every rectangular type. It follows from indifference read as genericity: the structure that a choice with no preference lands on with probability one for the invariant measure class. In this use, what the indifference premise (Principle \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series}) adds beyond symmetry is that measure principle.
synthesis.principality-is-genericity.technical: The series selects the principal embedding of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ into the boundary modes' matrix algebra by its indifference premise: other embeddings carry uncaused partition data. This result tests that selection against three precise readings of indifference. Invariance under the matrix algebra's own symmetry selects only the zero map, the one structure fixed by conjugation. Requiring that no block be distinguished from another allows every rectangular partition $(k^{n/k})$, since the commutant permutes equal blocks; for $n$ prime this leaves only the principal embedding and the zero map. Only genericity singles out the principal embedding: its orbit is the unique one of full dimension $n^2 - n$ in the nilpotent cone, so a choice with no preference, made with any measure in the invariant class, lands on it with probability one. In this use, indifference is a measure principle added to symmetry.
synthesis.principality-is-genericity.lay: The series picks one particular way for the symmetry of a sphere to act on the boundary modes, arguing that any other way would make arbitrary distinctions. This result asks which reading of "no arbitrary distinctions" actually makes that choice. Demanding full symmetry picks the trivial option where nothing acts at all. Demanding that no group of modes be singled out still allows several options when the number of modes can be split evenly. Only the reading "pick what a random choice gives almost surely" selects the series' option uniquely. So the premise is doing the work of a rule about probability, not just about symmetry.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} By Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-partition-data}(i), $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ structures on $\Mat_n$ (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}) are classified up to conjugation by the partition $\lambda$ of $n$ given by the restriction of the defining representation, $\C^n \cong \bigoplus_d V_d \otimes \C^{m_d}$ with $V_d$ the $d$-dimensional irreducible representation. In a basis adapted to the blocks the standard triple is $e_\lambda$ (one Jordan block of size $d$ per part), $h_\lambda = \bigoplus \operatorname{diag}(d-1, d-3, \dots, 1-d)$ and $f_\lambda$ with entries $(i+1)(d-1-i)$ below the diagonal of each block; then $[h,e] = 2e$, $[h,f] = -2f$, $[e,f] = h$, since the diagonal of $[e,f]$ in a block is $(i+1)(d-1-i) - i(d-i) = d-1-2i$. The check builds these triples exactly for every partition of every $n \leq 6$ and verifies the three relations.

\emph{(i).} The conjugation orbit of $e_\lambda$ is $GL_n/C(e_\lambda)$ with $C(e_\lambda)$ its centraliser, of dimension $n^2 - \dim C(e_\lambda)$. A matrix commuting with $e_\lambda$ is a module map of $\C^n$ over the polynomial ring in $e_\lambda$, and the maps from a Jordan block of size $a$ to one of size $b$ form a space of dimension $\min(a,b)$; so $\dim C(e_\lambda) = \sum_{a,b}\min(\lambda_a, \lambda_b) = \sum_i (\lambda^{T}_i)^2$, the last step counting, for each level $i$, the pairs of parts both exceeding $i$. The check \texttt{check\_principal\_is\_the\_unique\_full\_dimensional\_orbit} computes $\dim C(e_\lambda)$ as the nullity of $X \mapsto [X, e_\lambda]$ by exact rank and confirms the formula for every $\lambda$ with $n \leq 6$. The orbit is a point exactly when $C(e_\lambda) = \mathfrak{gl}_n$, that is when $e_\lambda$ is central and nilpotent, that is $e_\lambda = 0$, $\lambda = (1^n)$; then $h = [e,f] = 0$ and the triple is zero. Conversely an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ structure $\phi$ fixed pointwise by every conjugation, $\operatorname{Ad}_g \circ \phi = \phi$, has central image, and $\mathfrak{sl}_2 = [\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2]$ maps to zero in the abelian centre; so the zero map is the only structure that the symmetry of $\Mat_n$ fixes. The check confirms that $(1^n)$ is the only partition with orbit dimension $0$.

\emph{(ii).} By Schur's lemma the commutant of the image of the triple is $\bigoplus_d \mathfrak{gl}(m_d)$, acting on the multiplicity spaces, of dimension $\sum_d m_d^2$; the check computes it as the nullity of $X \mapsto ([X,e], [X,f])$ and confirms the formula for every $\lambda$ with $n \leq 6$. The group $GL(m_d)$ acts transitively on the decompositions of $V_d \otimes \C^{m_d}$ into $m_d$ copies of $V_d$ and contains the permutations of the copies in any one decomposition, so no block of size $d$ is distinguished from another of the same size; an equivariant automorphism preserves dimensions, so blocks of different sizes are always told apart. Hence no block is distinguished exactly when all parts are equal, $\lambda = (k^{n/k})$ with $k \mid n$. The check confirms, for $n \leq 6$, that the rectangular partitions are exactly those indexed by the divisors of $n$, that there are two of them, $(n)$ and $(1^n)$, exactly when $n$ is prime, and that $(2,2)$ at $n = 4$ has a four-dimensional commutant.

\emph{(iii).} $\sum_i (\lambda^{T}_i)^2 \geq \sum_i \lambda^{T}_i = n$, with equality exactly when every $\lambda^{T}_i = 1$, that is $\lambda^{T} = (1^n)$, $\lambda = (n)$; so the principal orbit has dimension $n^2 - n$ and every other orbit is strictly smaller, as the check confirms for $n \leq 6$. Every nilpotent matrix, real or complex, is conjugate to some $e_\lambda$ (its Jordan form; all dimensions here are over the ground field), so the nilpotent cone $\mathcal{N}$ is the finite union of the orbits $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$. The non-principal orbits form the closed set $\{x \in \mathcal{N} : x^{n-1} = 0\}$, so $\mathcal{O}_{(n)}$ is open in $\mathcal{N}$; it is dense, since adding $\varepsilon$ to the missing superdiagonal entries of $e_\lambda$ gives a strictly upper triangular matrix with nonzero superdiagonal, which is regular nilpotent, and tends to $e_\lambda$. The other orbits are submanifolds of dimension less than $n^2 - n$ and so have zero $(n^2 - n)$-dimensional measure; conjugation acts by diffeomorphisms, so the class of smooth positive densities on $\mathcal{O}_{(n)}$ is conjugation invariant, and every measure absolutely continuous with respect to it gives the type $(n)$ with probability one. Through the classification, a nilpotent element of type $(n)$ is the $e$ of the principal embedding.

\emph{Conclusion.} The three readings of indifference give three different answers: the zero map, the rectangular types, the principal embedding. Theorem \claimref{scrambling.principality-indifference-sphere} needs the third, which is a symmetry statement (the invariant measure class) together with a measure principle (a choice made without preference lands where that class puts full measure); the first two do not give it, the second failing for every composite $n$.

check_principal_is_the_unique_full_dimen.omits: Every partition of n for each n = 2..6 (exhaustive within that range, the statement is for all n): sl2 relations, centraliser dimension sum of squares of the conjugate partition, orbit dimension n^2 - n only for (n) and zero only for (1^n); the measure-theoretic conclusion (finitely many orbits, principal orbit open and dense, almost sure type (n)), the pointwise-Ad_g-fixed formulation and the n = 2 remark are not computed

check_indistinguishable_blocks_are_the_r.omits: Every partition for n = 2..6: commutant dimension equals the sum of squared multiplicities and the multiplicity-one-size (rectangular) types are the divisor types, two for n prime; that the commutant permutes blocks of one size transitively and tells different sizes apart is stated in the docstring and not tested (only dimension counts and (2,2) at n = 4)

judge.note: Exact rank computations over all partitions of n <= 6 confirm the orbit dimensions, the commutant dimensions and the list of rectangular types; the genericity (measure) step and the transitivity claim are not computed.
